name: Sharice Davids
page_title: Sharice Davids' Issue Positions (Political Courage Test)
on_the_ballot: Running, Democratic for U.S. House (KS) - District 3

positions.question: Do you support the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade?

evidence.text: "One year ago, the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade and upended lives across our nation. Here in Kansas, we turned our anger into action – but extreme efforts to take away our right to choose have not relented.We won’t quit standing up to them, either."
"Without Roe to protect us, our right to choose is on the ballot this fall. I’m proud to be the only candidate for #KS03 who will fight to protect your freedoms."
Rated 100% by Planned Parenthood Action Fund
Voted in favor of HR 8296 "Women's Health Protection Act of 2022"

positions.question: Do you support expanding federal funding to support social safety net programs such as Social Security and Medicare?

evidence.text: "Politicians with extreme views have unveiled a proposal that would slash Social Security benefits for 2.3 million Kansans. I’ll keep fighting against attempts to rip these Social Security benefits away from people who have earned them."
Rated 100% by Alliance for Retired Americans
Rated 100% by National Committee to Preserve Social Security and Medicare (NCPSM
Voted in favor of S 610 "Protecting Medicare and American Farmers from Sequester Cuts Act"

positions.question: Do you support the federal government increasing funding for affordable housing programs?

evidence.text: "In 2021, Kansas faced a shortage of 55K affordable rental homes for low-income renters. That's why I'm supporting @repcleaver’s Choice in Affordable Housing Act to expand access for KS families."
"I’m supporting the bipartisan bill Choice in Affordable Housing Act – to make sure all hardworking folks across Kansas can afford the adequate, safe housing they deserve."
Voted in favor of HR 7301 "Emergency Housing Protection and Relief Act of 2020"
Voted in favor of HR 8294 "Transportation, Housing and Urban Development, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2023"

positions.question: Do you support the federal government taking action, beyond those of the Federal Reserve, to alleviate inflation?

evidence.text: "Fighting inflation takes more than words - it takes action. That’s why I worked with the @NewDemCoalition to release a comprehensive blueprint on how to strengthen our global supply chain and make gas, groceries, and housing more affordable."

"Proud to be named to the conference committee and continue advancing legislation to fix our supply chains, reduce inflation, and make more here at home. I look forward to working with my House and Senate colleagues from both parties to get this done."
"The Chips and Science Act will help fix our supply chains, create good-paying jobs, tackle inflation, and improve America’s competitiveness."
Voted in favor of HR 5376 "Inflation Reduction Act of 2022"

positions.question: Do you generally support gun-control legislation (e.g. red flag laws, boyfriend loopholes)?

evidence.text: "How many mornings will we wake up to news of another mass shooting? How many families have to be ripped apart by gun violence? This can't be our new normal. In honor of the lives lost in Indianapolis and across the country to gun violence, the Senate must pass gun reforms."

"It’s been 161 days since the House passed H.R. 8, a bipartisan, common sense bill to institute universal background checks on gun purchases. And it's been 161 days of no action from Mitch McConnell. 161 days of more lives being cut short by gun violence. No more."
Rated 0% by the NRA
Voted in favor of HR 1808 "Assault Weapons Ban of 2022"

positions.question: Should the government be able to regulate the cost of prescription drugs?

evidence.text: "Kansans shouldn’t have to pay 3x what people in other countries pay for prescription drugs. A new law will put money back in your pocket by lowering the cost of medication. Today, I spoke with folks about what that relief means to them."
"No one should have to choose between paying for the prescriptions they need or paying for food or rent. We must allow Medicare to negotiate prescription drug prices."
"Prescription drug costs are too high. That’s why I helped pass a new law that allows Medicare to negotiate with Big Pharma for lower drug prices."

positions.question: Do you support increasing security along the southern US border?

Voted against HR 2 "Secure the Border Act of 2023"
